cases.prompt: Our OrderController returns the JPA Order entity directly and clients now see a LazyInitializationException on the lines collection plus a payload with createdAt and version in it. Fix it.
expectations: Names entity return from a controller as a boundary defect rather than a serialization bug
Lists lazy loading, N+1 queries, over-posting, schema leak, and unbounded payload as the failures
Introduces an OrderView record and explicit mapping instead of @JsonIgnore on the entity
Requires a fetch plan or a projection for the relation rather than relying on lazy loading during serialization

cases.prompt: Clients can set status, totalMinor, and ownerId on POST /orders by adding those keys to the JSON. Only clientReference, deliverAt, and lines are meant to be writable.
expectations: Recommends separate CreateOrderRequest, UpdateOrderRequest, and read model types
Builds a writable-field matrix that shows status, totalMinor, ownerId, version, and createdAt as server-owned on every operation
Explains that a deny-list breaks on the next schema change while an allow-listed record makes the field unbinding impossible
Warns against binding the request body onto a JPA entity or compensating with entity-level validation

cases.prompt: We now have 30 DTOs and hand-written mappers are missing fields. Should we add MapStruct, write static factories, or create a mapper component?
expectations: Recommends a generated mapper for many repetitive field-by-field copies and requires unmappedTargetPolicy set to ERROR
Lists server-owned target fields as explicit ignore mappings so the allow-list is visible in code
Suggests an explicit mapper component when lookups, conditionals, or multi-source composition are needed
Notes that a read model built by a projection query needs no mapper at all

cases.prompt: Our attachment endpoint returns a DTO with a byte[] content field. A test mutates the array after construction and the DTO changes too.
expectations: Identifies the missing defensive copy in the record as the defect
Clones the array in the compact constructor and overrides the accessor to return a clone
Applies the same rule to List, Set, and Map components with copyOf
Notes that immutability is per type, so nested records must copy their own structures

cases.prompt: We want to add an optional priority field to the order request DTO. Is that a breaking change for our clients?
expectations: Classifies a new optional field with a null default as additive for clients that ignore unknown fields
Notes it is breaking for clients that reject unknown fields or for strict deserializers
Requires the default to reproduce the previous server behavior and be pinned by a test
Hands the version decision for genuinely breaking changes to the API versioning skill

cases.prompt: We added SHIPPED to the orderStatus enum that clients receive. Existing generated clients will now fail to parse the new value. What should we have done?
expectations: Classifies adding an enum value as a breaking change for strict client deserializers
Explains the tolerant-client options such as an UNKNOWN value or an open string field
States that the type strictness decision sits in the DTO while the version decision belongs to the API versioning skill
Warns that a record component set to an enum also fails when Jackson encounters an unknown constant
